overview: Dominion Energy is a Richmond, Virginia-headquartered regulated utility holding company providing electricity to approximately 4.1 million customers in Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina through its Dominion Energy Virginia (Virginia Electric and Power Company), Dominion Energy South Carolina (DESC) and Contracted Energy (Millstone nuclear plus nonregulated renewables) segments. Roughly 95% of earnings come from state-regulated utility operations earning a cost-of-service return on a rapidly growing rate base, with the company in the midst of a ~$2.6 GW offshore wind build (Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind) and a surge in data-center-driven electricity demand in Northern Virginia. In May 2026 Dominion agreed to an all-stock merger with NextEra Energy (0.8138 NEE shares per Dominion share) that, if approved by regulators, would close in H2 2027 and make Dominion part of the largest regulated electric utility business by market capitalization.

business_model.summary: Cost-of-service regulated electric (and, in South Carolina, gas) utility earning an allowed return on equity on an expanding rate base, supplemented by a nonregulated long-term-contracted generation fleet (Millstone nuclear, solar, renewable natural gas). After divesting all non-DESC gas distribution operations to Enbridge in 2024 ($9.3bn total proceeds) and selling a 50% interest in the Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind (CVOW) project to Stonepeak, Dominion is now almost purely an electric-utility growth story funded by a $64.7bn 2026-2030 capital plan, with surging data-center demand in Virginia the primary growth driver.

revenue_streams.name: Dominion Energy Virginia (electric transmission, distribution, generation)
Dominion Energy South Carolina (electric + gas distribution)
Contracted Energy (Millstone nuclear, solar, renewable natural gas)
Corporate and Other / discontinued operations runoff

business_model.customer_type: Regulated B2C and B2B utility customer base - residential, commercial, industrial, governmental and a rapidly growing cohort of high-load data center customers (28% of Virginia Power's 2025 electricity sales, up from 26% in 2024)
business_model.geographic_mix: Virginia and North Carolina (Dominion Energy Virginia, ~80% of revenue from Virginia jurisdiction), South Carolina (Dominion Energy South Carolina), Connecticut (Millstone nuclear within Contracted Energy)

competitive_position.market_position: Exclusive franchised monopoly for electric transmission and distribution within its Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina service territories; one of the largest developers of offshore wind and solar in the U.S. and the largest producer of carbon-free electricity in New England (Millstone)

moat_factors.description: No competition permitted for electric distribution service in Virginia Power's or DESC's territories; CPCN requirements and state commission approval needed for new generation and large transmission lines
Allowed ROE on a rapidly growing, regulator-approved capital base provides predictable, largely de-risked earnings growth tied to the $64.7bn 2026-2030 capex plan
30.7 GW of generation, 10,800 miles of transmission and 80,400 miles of distribution lines create high barriers to entry and switching costs for load customers

moat_factors.factor: Concentration of hyperscale data center demand
moat_factors.description: Loudoun County, Virginia's unique data-center cluster gives Dominion a captive, high-growth demand base, though it also concentrates execution and credit risk

weaknesses: Order 1000 permits non-incumbent transmission owners (e.g., AEP, FirstEnergy via the Valley Link joint venture) to compete for new transmission build in Dominion's territory
Some large Virginia jurisdictional customers can shop for 100%-renewable competitive generation suppliers
DESC's natural gas distribution customers can switch to alternative fuels (propane, fuel oil) on price
Heavy reliance on continued data-center load growth that is itself uncertain and politically contested (cost-allocation disputes)
Pending NextEra merger caps independent strategic flexibility and standalone equity upside pending deal completion

growth_drivers: Data-center and AI-driven electricity demand in Virginia; PJM projects 5.4% average annual peak load growth over the next decade for the PJM DOM Zone
~$64.7 billion 2026-2030 capital expenditure plan ("all-of-the-above" strategy) spanning generation, grid transformation, transmission and distribution resiliency
Completion of the 2.6 GW Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind (CVOW) Commercial Project, with first power delivered March 2026 and full completion targeted by end of 2027
New dispatchable natural gas generation (Chesterfield Energy Reliability Center, ~944 MW) and continued utility-scale solar and battery storage builds (~$6.9bn solar, ~$2.0bn storage, 2026-2030)
Nuclear license extensions (Surry, North Anna through 2052-2060; pursuing Millstone extensions to 2055/2065) preserving low-cost, carbon-free baseload
Valley Link transmission joint venture with AEP and FirstEnergy to serve PJM-driven regional transmission needs

Pending all-stock combination with NextEra Energy, which would create the largest regulated electric utility by market capitalization and improved credit outlook (Moody's, S&P and Fitch all moved to positive outlook/watch in May 2026 following the merger announcement)

business.description: A large share of projected load growth depends on continued hyperscale data-center build-out; project cancellations, AI capex pullbacks or customers moving load elsewhere could leave Dominion with stranded infrastructure investment despite new 14-year minimum-demand contract protections beginning January 2027

Large, complex $11.7bn offshore wind project; subject to weather, vessel availability, tariffs, supply-chain and regulatory risk, with a cost-sharing/disallowance mechanism above $10.3bn and no recovery mechanism above $13.7bn
Storm restoration costs and SAIDI reliability metrics have trended worse in recent years, with associated capital and O&M cost pressure

business.risk: Fuel mix / coal and nuclear transition
business.description: Residual coal generation (DESC ~23% of output) and long-dated nuclear decommissioning liabilities (Surry, North Anna, Summer, Millstone) carry environmental and funding risk

financial.risk: High leverage and heavy external financing needs
financial.description: Plans to issue $6.0-9.5bn of long-term debt in 2026 alone plus ~$1.6-1.8bn of equity issuance to fund the capital plan; total debt-to-capital at 53.5% against a 67.5% covenant maximum

Heavy reliance on debt markets for a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar capital program makes earnings and financing costs sensitive to rate levels; a 10% rise in rates would reduce Dominion Energy's variable-rate earnings by about $14 million and swing fixed-income derivative fair values materially

financial.risk: Foreign currency exposure on CVOW contracts
financial.description: Fixed-price CVOW construction contracts denominated in Euros and Danish kroner are partially but not fully hedged via forward purchase agreements

financial.risk: Dividend/distribution restrictions under the NextEra merger agreement
financial.description: The merger agreement now restricts certain dividend and capital-return actions pending closing

regulatory.description: Closing requires approval from the Virginia SCC, North Carolina and South Carolina commissions, FERC (Section 203), NRC and HSR antitrust clearance; Virginia's Lt. Governor has pushed for an extensive pre-review questionnaire, and data-center cost-allocation politics could complicate or delay approval; an undisclosed rival bidder ("Party A") previously approached Dominion

Virginia Power's earned ROE and rate base are reset every two years by the Virginia Commission (next full review period 2025-2026, with the 2027 Biennial Review covering 2025-2026); adverse findings could trigger customer refunds
EPA's September 2026 repeal of most of the 2024 CO2 rules for fossil generation creates planning uncertainty; future rulemaking could still impose material compliance costs

regulatory.risk: FERC/PJM market design and capacity cost allocation changes
regulatory.description: FERC's 2024 PJM capacity market order and evolving network-upgrade cost allocation (including costs assigned to CVOW and new generation) could adversely affect recoverable revenue

macro.description: As a capital-intensive regulated utility financing a $65bn multi-year plan, Dominion is more rate-sensitive than most sectors; higher-for-longer rates raise financing costs and can compress equity valuations of bond-proxy utility stocks

Steel, aluminum, copper and transportation-fuel tariffs (Section 232 and related actions) have already added hundreds of millions of dollars to CVOW's estimated cost and could affect other capital projects
A slowdown in AI/data-center capital spending nationally could reduce the pace of Virginia load growth underpinning Dominion's rate-base growth thesis

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. regulated utilities are seeing their best demand-growth backdrop in decades, driven by data centers, electrification and reshoring manufacturing; PJM's DOM Zone (Dominion Energy Virginia) is at the epicenter given its concentration of hyperscale data centers in Loudoun County
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low - regulated cost-of-service revenue is largely non-cyclical, though weather and, to a lesser extent, economic activity affect usage-based sales
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - capital-intensive multi-year build plan funded substantially with debt and equity issuance makes earnings, financing costs and the stock's valuation (bond-proxy characteristics) sensitive to interest rates

recent_developments.event: Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy announced a definitive agreement for an all-stock merger (0.8138 NEE shares per Dominion share, ~$66.8bn deal value), creating what the companies describe as the world's largest regulated electric utility business by market capitalization; expected to close H2 2027 subject to regulatory approval

Moody's, S&P and Fitch all revised Dominion Energy's credit outlook to positive (Fitch to positive watch) following the merger announcement, having previously carried a negative (Moody's) or stable outlook

Dominion and NextEra filed joint merger applications with the Virginia SCC, North Carolina and South Carolina commissions, FERC and the NRC; the deal also includes a proposed $2.25bn in customer bill credits across Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina over two years post-closing

Shareholders of both Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy approved the merger; regulatory approvals (including Virginia SCC review, complicated by political scrutiny of data-center cost allocation) remain outstanding

CVOW Commercial Project delivered first power to the grid in March 2026 after a temporary BOEM-ordered work suspension (Dec 2025-Jan 2026) was lifted by a federal court injunction; project now ~85% complete with 44 of 176 turbines installed as of October 2026 and full completion targeted by end of 2027

Q3 2026 results: operating EPS of $1.28 (vs. $1.06 prior year, beating the $1.21 consensus estimate); GAAP EPS of $1.30; company reaffirmed full-year 2026 operating EPS guidance of $3.45-$3.69 and said it expects to land in the top half of that range; YTD operating EPS of $3.02 vs. $2.74 a year earlier

The companies identified an immaterial misstatement related to deferred taxes on nuclear decommissioning trust investments, requiring revision of previously issued 2023-2024 financial statements (no impact on cash flows or overall financial condition)
EPA finalized a rule repealing most of the May 2024 CO2 emissions rules for fossil-fuel generating units, reducing near-term compliance cost pressure but adding regulatory uncertainty

items.notes: Company stated it expects results in the top half of the range after a Q3 beat ($1.28 vs. $1.21 consensus)
Tied to the 2026-2030 capital plan and rate-base growth

items.target: $64.7 billion (updated from $65.7bn to reflect Stonepeak's 50% noncontrolling interest in CVOW)
items.notes: Dominion Energy Virginia ~$55.8bn, Dominion Energy South Carolina ~$7.6bn, Contracted Energy ~$1.7bn, Corporate and Other ~$0.6bn
Consistent with the 2025 rate; now also subject to restrictions under the NextEra merger agreement
To fund capex (net of Stonepeak CVOW reimbursements) and debt maturities; $6.7bn already issued through Q3 2026

items.target: ~$1.6-$1.8 billion via at-the-market programs (excl. opportunistic offerings), plus ~$150 million via Dominion Energy Direct/employee plans
items.notes: Includes ~$1.0bn from settlement of previously executed forward sale agreements; no open-market share buybacks planned in 2026

guidance.management_commentary: Management reaffirmed the FY2026 operating EPS range and the 5%-7% long-term growth rate, and said it expects to finish 2026 in the top half of guidance after data-center-driven sales growth and favorable weather. The NextEra Energy merger dominates forward commentary: management emphasized no material change to the 2026 standalone outlook, continued progress toward CVOW completion by end of 2027, and the expectation that the combination closes in the second half of 2027 pending the outstanding state and federal regulatory approvals.

bull_case: Pending all-stock merger with NextEra Energy, if completed, converts Dominion into part of the largest regulated U.S. utility by market cap, with the merger announcement already driving credit rating outlooks to positive across all three agencies

Dominion Energy Virginia sits at the epicenter of U.S. data-center/AI electricity demand growth (PJM projects 5.4% annual peak load growth in the DOM Zone), supporting a long runway of regulator-approved rate-base growth and 5-7% long-term operating EPS growth guidance

CVOW, the largest U.S. offshore wind project, is now de-risked and ~85% complete with first power already delivered, removing much of the multi-year construction/financing overhang as it nears its end-2027 completion
New 14-year minimum-demand, collateralized contract terms for high-load (data center) customers effective January 2027 reduce stranded-cost risk from speculative or cancelled projects
Regulated, monopoly franchise cash flows and large embedded capital program provide earnings visibility largely insulated from economic cycles
bear_case: The fixed 0.8138 NEE exchange ratio caps Dominion's standalone upside - the stock now effectively trades as a function of NextEra's share price plus a deal-completion/timing discount, with consensus analyst ratings clustered at Hold and price targets well below where a successful deal plus premium might otherwise imply

Merger completion is not guaranteed: it requires sign-off from the Virginia SCC, North Carolina and South Carolina commissions, FERC, the NRC and HSR antitrust clearance, against a backdrop of political scrutiny over data-center cost allocation and a reported rival bidder ("Party A") that could complicate the process or signal latent deal risk

Heavy reliance on continued hyperscale data-center load growth; any slowdown in AI/data-center capex nationally or project cancellations would undercut the core growth thesis embedded in the $64.7bn capital plan

Elevated leverage and a multi-year need to issue $6-9.5bn of debt and ~$1.6-1.8bn of equity annually leave Dominion exposed to higher-for-longer interest rates, which raise financing costs and pressure bond-proxy utility valuations

CVOW remains subject to residual execution, tariff and weather risk before full completion, with limited cost recovery above $13.7bn in total project costs and performance-based remedies if capacity factors disappoint
